checks.label: Boot Mode Status
checks.description: Device boot mode - fastboot/recovery/charger modes allow partition modification
checks.remediation: Reboot the device normally. If stuck in recovery or fastboot, investigate the cause before rebooting.

checks.label: vbmeta Device State
checks.description: vbmeta device_state must be locked
checks.remediation: Re-lock the bootloader via 'fastboot flashing lock' after flashing stock firmware.

checks.label: AVB Version Present
checks.description: AVB version should be present
checks.remediation: Ensure the device firmware includes AVB support. Flash a firmware build that ships with vbmeta.

checks.label: avbctl Present
checks.command: command -v avbctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo present || echo absent
checks.description: avbctl binary available for rollback checks
checks.remediation: Install or restore the avbctl binary from the vendor partition or OEM system image.

checks.label: Rollback Index (slot 0) > 0
checks.command: command -v avbctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && avbctl get-rollback-index 0 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}' || echo 0
checks.description: Anti-rollback index should be > 0 (slot 0) (INFO if avbctl unavailable)
checks.remediation: Apply the latest OTA update to advance the rollback index. Ensure avbctl is available on the device.

checks.label: Rollback Index (slot 1) > 0
checks.command: command -v avbctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && avbctl get-rollback-index 1 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}' || echo 0
checks.description: Anti-rollback index should be > 0 (slot 1) (INFO if avbctl unavailable)
checks.remediation: Apply the latest OTA update to advance the rollback index. Ensure avbctl is available on the device.

checks.label: OEM Unlock Allowed
checks.description: Should be disabled to prevent unlock
checks.remediation: Disable OEM unlocking in Settings > Developer Options > OEM Unlocking.

checks.label: Safe Mode
checks.description: Should not be running in Safe Mode
checks.remediation: Reboot the device normally to exit Safe Mode.

checks.label: FRP Policy
checks.description: Factory Reset Protection should be enabled
checks.remediation: Add a Google account and enable FRP via device policy or MDM to protect against unauthorized resets.

checks.label: ADB Over Wi-Fi
checks.description: Risky if enabled
checks.remediation: Disable wireless debugging in Settings > Developer Options > Wireless Debugging.

checks.label: Bootloader Locked
checks.description: 1 means locked bootloader; 0 means unlocked
checks.remediation: Re-lock the bootloader via 'fastboot flashing lock' after restoring stock firmware.

checks.label: OEM Unlock Hardware Capability
checks.description: Reports ro.oem_unlock_supported, which states whether the hardware exposes an OEM unlock path at all. This is a device capability, not a security state: the large majority of non-carrier-locked devices report 1 and are perfectly secure with the bootloader locked. It was previously scored critical against a safe_pattern of ^0$, so nearly every device raised a critical finding for supporting a feature it ships with. The security-relevant facts are covered by 'Bootloader Locked' (ro.boot.flash.locked), 'OEM Unlock Allowed' (sys.oem_unlock_allowed) and 'OEM Unlock Permitted (Global Setting)'.
checks.remediation: Nothing to act on directly. Confirm the bootloader is locked and that OEM unlocking is not permitted; those are the checks that matter.

checks.label: OEM Unlock Permitted (Global Setting)
checks.command: A=$(settings get global oem_unlock_allowed 2>/dev/null); B=$(settings get global oem_unlock_enabled 2>/dev/null); V="$A"; [ -z "$V" ] || [ "$V" = "null" ] && V="$B"; case "${V:-null}" in 1) echo "UNLOCK_PERMITTED allowed=${A:-null} enabled=${B:-null}";; 0) echo "UNLOCK_BLOCKED allowed=${A:-null} enabled=${B:-null}";; *) echo "NOT_SET allowed=${A:-null} enabled=${B:-null}";; esac
checks.description: Reports whether the OEM unlocking toggle in Developer Options permits the bootloader to be unlocked. Both spellings of the key are read, because oem_unlock_allowed and oem_unlock_enabled are used by different OEM builds and a check reading only one returns null on the other. NOT_SET is treated as passing because neither key present means the toggle was never enabled. This merges two checks that read one spelling each and reported the same fact at different severities.
checks.remediation: Turn off OEM unlocking in Developer Options. On a managed fleet, block it with the DevicePolicyManager OEM-unlock restriction so a local user cannot re-enable it.

checks.label: FRP Partition Path Set
checks.description: Factory Reset Protection partition path configured
checks.remediation: Ensure the device tree defines ro.frp.pst pointing to the persistent storage partition for FRP.

checks.label: dm-verity Mode and Source Consistency
checks.command: C=$(grep -hoE 'androidboot\.veritymode[ ]*=[ ]*"?[a-z_]+' /proc/cmdline /proc/bootconfig 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[a-z_]+$' | head -1); P=$(getprop ro.boot.veritymode 2>/dev/null); M=${C:-$P}; SRC=cmdline; [ -z "$C" ] && SRC=property; if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo 'UNVERIFIABLE no veritymode from cmdline, bootconfig or property'; elif [ -n "$C" ] && [ -n "$P" ] && [ "$C" != "$P" ]; then echo "MISMATCH cmdline=$C prop=$P"; else case "$M" in enforcing|eio|restart|panicking) echo "VERITY_OK mode=$M source=$SRC";; *) echo "VERITY_WEAK mode=$M source=$SRC";; esac; fi
checks.description: Reports the dm-verity error-handling mode and cross-checks the two places it is published. The bootloader writes androidboot.veritymode into the kernel command line and bootconfig, which userspace cannot rewrite, while ro.boot.veritymode is a property that resetprop can change. VERITY_OK means the mode is one of enforcing, eio, restart or panicking. MISMATCH means the command line and the property disagree, which is proof the property has been forged. VERITY_WEAK means verity is present but set to a non-enforcing mode such as logging or disabled. This merges two checks that read the same fact from the two sources independently and each scored critical, so a single misconfiguration produced two findings and a spoofed property produced none.
checks.remediation: Restore an enforcing verity mode by reflashing stock vbmeta without the disable-verity flag. On MISMATCH, find and remove the property-spoofing module before trusting any other property-derived check.

checks.label: dm-verity-backed Partitions Mounted
checks.description: At least one partition should be backed by dm-verity
checks.remediation: Reflash stock firmware and vbmeta to restore dm-verity-backed partition mounts.

checks.label: AVB/Verity Success in dmesg
checks.description: Kernel logs should show AVB/verity success (if accessible)
checks.remediation: Verify dmesg access permissions. Reflash stock images if AVB/verity messages are absent.

checks.label: Test-keys Build
checks.description: Test-keys in fingerprint indicates insecure engineering/debug build
checks.remediation: Flash an official release-signed firmware build from the OEM. Do not use test-keys builds in production.

checks.label: Init Files Metadata Snapshot
checks.description: Informational snapshot of /init and /init.rc file metadata (size, mtime, mode). Note: this does NOT detect tampering by itself; it captures filesystem metadata for post-audit review. For real tampering detection, compare against a known-good hash (see dm-verity / Verified Boot checks elsewhere in this category).
checks.remediation: Compare /init and /init.rc sizes and timestamps against known-good stock images for anomalies.

checks.label: app_process Filesystem Attributes
checks.description: Informational snapshot of lsattr output on app_process* binaries (which are the Zygote entry points). Note: this does NOT detect tampering by itself; it captures filesystem extended attributes (e.g. immutable bit) for post-audit review.
checks.remediation: Reflash the stock system image if unexpected attributes are found on app_process binaries.

checks.label: VBMeta Digest (verified-boot fingerprint)
checks.command: D=$(getprop ro.boot.vbmeta.digest 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$D" ]; then D=$(grep -hoE 'androidboot\.vbmeta\.digest=[a-f0-9]+|androidboot\.vbmeta\.digest = "[a-f0-9]+' /proc/cmdline /proc/bootconfig 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[a-f0-9]+$' | head -1); fi; echo "$D"
checks.description: AVB VBMeta digest - a SHA-256/512 hash over all vbmeta structs (including chained partitions). It is the runtime fingerprint of the entire verified-boot metadata and the value used in hardware-backed attestation. Record it per firmware build and diff across audits to detect vbmeta tampering. Empty means the bootloader did not export it (non-AVB or older device).
checks.remediation: Record this digest per firmware build as a known-good baseline. A change on the same build indicates vbmeta was modified - reflash stock vbmeta with 'fastboot flash vbmeta vbmeta.img'. With --save-baseline / --baseline this comparison is automatic.

checks.label: dm-verity Managed Error-Mode Policy
checks.command: M=$(grep -hoE 'androidboot\.veritymode\.managed=[a-z]+|androidboot\.veritymode\.managed = "[a-z]+' /proc/cmdline /proc/bootconfig 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[a-z]+$' | head -1); I=$(grep -hoE 'androidboot\.vbmeta\.invalidate_on_error=[a-z]+|androidboot\.vbmeta\.invalidate_on_error = "[a-z]+' /proc/cmdline /proc/bootconfig 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[a-z]+$' | head -1); echo "managed=${M:-unset} invalidate_on_error=${I:-unset}"
checks.description: Records the AVB hashtree error-handling policy (androidboot.veritymode.managed and androidboot.vbmeta.invalidate_on_error). 'managed=yes' is the recommended AVB_HASHTREE_ERROR_MODE_MANAGED_RESTART_AND_EIO state machine for Android; 'invalidate_on_error=yes' corresponds to RESTART_AND_INVALIDATE. Informational - pair with the 'Verity Mode' checks to confirm verity fails closed.
checks.remediation: For Android devices use AVB_HASHTREE_ERROR_MODE_MANAGED_RESTART_AND_EIO so corruption triggers a managed restart/EIO rather than serving corrupt data.

checks.label: VBMeta Hash Algorithm Not Weak
checks.description: Hash algorithm protecting the top-level vbmeta struct. sha1 is cryptographically weak for verified boot; modern devices use sha256 or sha512. Empty/unset on devices that do not export the property.
checks.remediation: Rebuild and flash vbmeta signed with a SHA-256 or SHA-512 algorithm (set BOARD_AVB_ALGORITHM to e.g. SHA256_RSA4096 or SHA512_RSA4096).

checks.label: Kernel CONFIG_DM_VERITY_AVB Support
checks.description: CONFIG_DM_VERITY_AVB lets the kernel invalidate the current slot on dm-verity corruption, required for AVB_HASHTREE_ERROR_MODE_RESTART_AND_INVALIDATE. 'absent' means /proc/config.gz is not exposed (common) - this is informational, not a failure.
checks.remediation: If using the RESTART_AND_INVALIDATE error mode, build the kernel with CONFIG_DM_VERITY_AVB=y. Not required for EIO/managed modes.

checks.label: VBMeta Size Baseline
checks.description: Size in bytes of the verified vbmeta blob, exported by the bootloader. Record alongside the VBMeta digest as a known-good baseline; an unexpected change on the same firmware build is a tamper indicator. Empty on devices that do not export it.
checks.remediation: Informational baseline. Capture per firmware build and compare across audits (use --save-baseline / --baseline).

checks.label: Required libavb Version (vbmeta)
checks.description: libavb version required to verify the vbmeta struct (distinct from ro.boot.avb_version). Informational - confirms the vbmeta was AVB-verified and records the version for fleet consistency.
checks.remediation: Informational. Ensure the bootloader's libavb version matches the version avbtool used to sign the images.

checks.label: Verified Boot Custom Root of Trust (verifiedbootstate=yellow)
checks.command: V=$(grep -hoE 'androidboot\.verifiedbootstate=[a-z]+|androidboot\.verifiedbootstate = "[a-z]+' /proc/cmdline /proc/bootconfig 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[a-z]+$' | head -1); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop ro.boot.verifiedbootstate 2>/dev/null); case "$V" in yellow) echo "YELLOW_CUSTOM_ROOT_OF_TRUST" ;; *) echo "OK_${V:-unset}" ;; esac
checks.description: verifiedbootstate=yellow means the bootloader is LOCKED but boots an OS signed with a user-installed custom root of trust (a custom AVB key, e.g. one flashed to avb_custom_key). Verified boot is still enforced, but by a non-OEM key, so a custom or potentially unauthorized build is running under a locked bootloader. This is distinct from orange (fully UNLOCKED), which the 'vbmeta Device State', 'Bootloader Locked' and 'verifiedbootstate=green' checks already flag as critical - yellow is surfaced here as a warning so a custom-key deployment is not conflated with an unlocked device. Only 'yellow' fails this check. Reads /proc/cmdline, /proc/bootconfig (Android 12+) and getprop.
checks.remediation: If a custom root of trust is not expected on this fleet, reflash OEM-signed firmware and remove the custom AVB key (e.g. 'fastboot erase avb_custom_key' on Pixel). If the custom key is intentional (an in-house signed build), record it as the expected state and baseline the root-of-trust fingerprint.

checks.label: Protected KVM / AVF Support (pKVM)
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.boot.hypervisor.protected_vm.supported 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop ro.boot.hypervisor.version 2>/dev/null); N=$(getprop ro.boot.hypervisor.vm.supported 2>/dev/null); echo "protected_vm=${S:-unset} vm=${N:-unset} hypervisor=${V:-none}"
checks.description: Protected KVM (pKVM) is Android's hypervisor for the Android Virtualization Framework (AVF): it runs isolated protected VMs whose memory even a fully compromised Android kernel cannot read. It underpins Isolated Compilation, on-device Private Compute workloads and, on Android 17, AISeal (hardware-backed isolation for Private AI Compute). protected_vm=1 means the device boot-advertises pKVM protected-VM support (SAFE); unset/0 means the SoC or firmware does not expose it, which is the norm on most non-Pixel and older hardware and is reported as INFO rather than a failure. The hypervisor version string, when present, identifies the AVF generation.
checks.remediation: Nothing to fix on existing hardware; pKVM support is fixed by SoC and firmware. For high-assurance refresh cycles (devices processing sensitive data on-device, or Android 17 AI privacy features), prefer hardware that advertises protected_vm=1.

checks.label: Verified Boot State Consistency (property vs kernel cmdline)
checks.command: P=$(getprop ro.boot.verifiedbootstate 2>/dev/null); C=$(cat /proc/cmdline /proc/bootconfig 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'androidboot\.verifiedbootstate[ ]*=[ ]*"?[a-z]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[a-z]+$'); L=$(getprop ro.boot.flash.locked 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$C" ]; then V=UNVERIFIABLE_NO_BOOT_CMDLINE; elif [ -z "$P" ]; then V=UNVERIFIABLE_NO_PROP; elif [ "$P" != "$C" ]; then V=MISMATCH_PROP_VS_CMDLINE; elif [ "$P" = "green" ] && [ "$L" = "0" ]; then V=MISMATCH_GREEN_BUT_UNLOCKED; else V=CONSISTENT; fi; echo "$V prop=${P:-unset} cmdline=${C:-unset} flash_locked=${L:-unset}"
checks.description: Property spoofing modules rewrite ro.boot.verifiedbootstate to 'green' with resetprop so that on-device integrity checks read a healthy value. They cannot rewrite the kernel command line: /proc/cmdline and /proc/bootconfig are populated by the bootloader before Android starts and are not writable from userspace. This check reads the same fact from both sources and compares them. A disagreement is direct, non-inferential proof that the boot state property has been forged. It also flags the contradictory combination of verifiedbootstate=green with flash.locked=0, which cannot occur on an honest device. This check does not judge whether the device is locked, that is the job of the separate Bootloader Locked and Verified Boot State checks. It only reports whether the device is telling the same story twice. An honestly unlocked device reports CONSISTENT here and is flagged by those other checks instead. Devices that expose neither source report UNVERIFIABLE and are not failed on absence of evidence.
checks.remediation: Identify and remove the module rewriting the boot properties, typically a resetprop-based Play Integrity or attestation spoofing module under /data/adb/modules. Reboot and re-run this check. Treat every prior on-device integrity decision made on this device as unreliable.
checks.why: The kernel command line cannot be rewritten from userspace, so a mismatch against the property is proof of deliberate boot state forgery.
checks.risk_if_fail: The device reports a forged verified boot state, so any local integrity check reading only the property is defeated.

checks.label: Security Patch Level Consistency
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop ro.vendor.build.security_patch 2>/dev/null); B=$(getprop ro.build.date.utc 2>/dev/null); D=$(getprop ro.build.date 2>/dev/null); echo "system_spl=${S:-unset} vendor_spl=${V:-unset} build_utc=${B:-unset} build_date=${D:-unset}"
checks.description: Attestation and integrity spoofing tooling commonly forges the security patch level alongside the boot state, so that a device running an outdated build advertises a current patch date. This collects the system patch level, the vendor patch level, and the build date for comparison. Two signals matter on review. A security patch level dated after the build date is impossible on an honest device, because a build cannot ship a patch that did not exist when it was compiled. A large gap between the system and vendor patch levels indicates a partial or forged update. Reported at verify level rather than as an automatic failure because the comparison needs date arithmetic that is not portable across the shells found on Android, and because a modest system-to-vendor skew is normal on real firmware.
checks.remediation: Compare system_spl against build_date. If the patch level is newer than the build date, the value is forged: locate and remove the spoofing module. If both are genuine but old, apply the vendor OTA to bring the device to a current patch level.
